im-c48-01.h: -아/어 보이다 (Visual Impression) vs -(으)ㄴ/는 모양이다 (Inference from Clues)

a.d: Used to describe what someone or something looks like based on what you directly see right in front of you.
ex: 얼굴이 창백해서 오늘 좀 **아파 보여요**. — You look a bit sick today because your face is pale.

b.d: Used to infer or deduce another person's situation or external events from visible traces, signs, or evidence.
ex: 불이 꺼진 걸 보니 사무실에 아무도 **없는 모양이에요**. — Seeing the lights are off, there must be no one in the office.

im-c48-01.tip: Use -아/어 보이다 for immediate look/appearance; use -(으)ㄴ/는 모양이다 when putting clues together to guess a hidden fact. Never use -(으)ㄴ/는 모양이다 for yourself.

im-c48-01.q: Fix the unnatural sentence that incorrectly uses -(으)ㄴ/는 모양이다 to talk about one's own internal feeling.
im-c48-01.wrong: 제가 배가 고픈 모양이에요. 밥 먹으러 가요.
answers: 제가 배가 너무 고파요. 밥 먹으러 가요.
제가 배가 고파요. 밥 먹으러 가요
배가 고파요. 밥 먹으러 가요.
배가 고파요. 밥 먹으러 가요
im-c48-01.hint: You directly feel your own hunger, so state it directly: 배가 너무 고파요.
im-c48-01.why: -(으)ㄴ/는 모양이다 is an inference based on clues and is never used to guess one's own immediate sensations.

items.ex: 비가 온 흔적이 곳곳에 남아 있어요.

im-c48-02.h: -(으)ㄹ 텐데 (Considerate Care) vs -(으)ㄹ 테니까 (Promised Action / Reason)

a.d: Used to express empathetic concern or provide background context for a suggestion/consolation.
ex: 많이 **바쁘실 텐데** 귀한 시간 내주셔서 감사합니다. — You must be very busy, thank you for sparing valuable time.

b.h: -(으)ㄹ 테니까 (Promising one's role or stating confirmed condition)
b.d: Used when volunteering to handle one part of a task, followed by an instruction, request, or proposal to the listener.
ex: 제가 회의실을 **예약할 테니까** 지수 씨는 자료를 준비해 주세요. — I will reserve the meeting room, so please prepare the materials.

im-c48-02.tip: Follow -(으)ㄹ 텐데 with consolation or care; follow -(으)ㄹ 테니까 with requests, commands, or suggestions (-(으)세요, -(으)ㅂ시다).

im-c48-02.q: Fix the awkward sentence when dividing work tasks with a partner.

answers: 제가 발표 자료를 만들 테니까 지수 씨는 발표를 맡아 주세요.
제가 발표 자료를 만들 테니까 지수 씨는 발표를 맡아 주세요
제가 발표 자료를 준비할 테니까 지수 씨는 발표를 맡아 주세요.
제가 발표 자료를 준비할 테니까 지수 씨는 발표를 맡아 주세요
im-c48-02.hint: When stating your promised contribution to prompt partner action, use -(으)ㄹ 테니까: 만들 테니까 지수 씨는...
im-c48-02.why: Committing one's action as the condition for a request requires -(으)ㄹ 테니까 rather than -(으)ㄹ 텐데.

The roads will freeze solid and driving would be dangerous, so using public transit is much safer.

im-c48-02.q: Why does the speaker recommend public transit instead of driving?

im-c48-02.q: What supportive action does the speaker volunteer to do for their colleague?
options: Share an umbrella walking to the subway station (우산을 씌워 드릴 테니까)
Buy a car for the colleague

items: I can preface friendly suggestions with considerate empathy using -(으)ㄹ 텐데.
I can assign roles and coordinate collaborative tasks smoothly using -(으)ㄹ 테니까.

a.d: Used when gently offering a reasonably confident guess, often slightly correcting what the listener assumed.
ex: 지금 가면 식당 문을 벌써 **닫았을걸요**. — If you go now, the restaurant is probably already closed.

b.d: Used when an outcome is not certain but cannot be ruled out, advising precaution just in case.
ex: 오후에 소나기가 **내릴지도 몰라요**. — It might shower this afternoon, so take an umbrella.

im-c48-03.tip: Use -(으)ㄹ걸요 for plausible hunches ('I bet...'); use -(으)ㄹ지도 몰라요 for unpredictable risks ('might / could').

im-c48-03.q: Fix the sentence advising someone to pack an umbrella for an unpredictable chance of rain.
im-c48-03.wrong: 오후에 비가 올걸요 미리 우산을 챙기세요.
answers: 오후에 비가 올지도 모르니까 미리 우산을 챙기세요.
오후에 비가 올지도 모르니까 미리 우산을 챙기세요
오후에 비가 올지도 모르니 미리 우산을 챙기세요.
오후에 비가 올지도 모르니 미리 우산을 챙기세요
im-c48-03.hint: To warn about an uncertain possibility so someone can prepare, use -(으)ㄹ지도 모르다: 비가 올지도 모르니까...
im-c48-03.why: Advising precaution for uncertain contingencies requires -(으)ㄹ지도 모르다, whereas -(으)ㄹ걸요 is a casual conclusion.

im-c48-03.say: 지금 출발해도 퇴근 시간이라 길이 많이 막힐걸요

im-c48-03.why: Gentle confident presumption with rising nuance: 막힐걸요.

im-c48-03.q: Write a considerate sentence telling your friend to head out first because you might be late, using 혹시 늦을지도 모르니까 and 먼저 출발하세요.

im-c48-04.h: -(으)ㄹ 텐데 (Caring Perspective) vs -(으)ㄹ 테니까 (Active Division of Work)

a.d: Used in polite requests to acknowledge the other person's burden or circumstances first.
ex: 먼 길 오시느라 **힘드셨을 텐데** 편안한 자리에 앉으세요. — It must have been tiring traveling such a long way, please take a comfortable seat.

b.d: Used in collaborative settings to proactively declare your task, making the colleague's role clear and easy.
ex: 제가 회의록을 **정리할 테니까** 팀장님께는 과장님이 보고해 주세요. — I will organize the meeting notes, so please report to the team leader, Manager.

im-c48-04.tip: Start with -(으)ㄹ 텐데 to soften requests respectfully; use -(으)ㄹ 테니까 to take charge of your part and guide teamwork.

im-c48-04.q: Fix the unnatural sentence when dividing responsibilities during team preparation.
im-c48-04.wrong: 제가 회의실을 정리할 텐데 지훈 씨는 손님을 배웅해 주세요.
answers: 제가 회의실을 정리할 테니까 지훈 씨는 손님을 배웅해 주세요.
제가 회의실을 정리할 테니까 지훈 씨는 손님을 배웅해 주세요
제가 회의실을 치울 테니까 지훈 씨는 손님을 배웅해 주세요.
제가 회의실을 치울 테니까 지훈 씨는 손님을 배웅해 주세요
im-c48-04.hint: Promising to handle room cleanup to ask Jihoon to see guests off takes -(으)ㄹ 테니까: 정리할 테니까 지훈 씨는...
im-c48-04.why: Volunteering an action as the reason for asking someone to do something requires -(으)ㄹ 테니까.

steps.en: You must have been very tired, please drink warm tea and rest comfortably.

tokens: 먼 길 찾아오시느라 많이 힘드셨을 텐데

steps.en: You must have been very tired coming from afar, so please sit by the window with warm tea and rest comfortably.

ko: 외부 귀빈들이 우리 사무실을 방문하셨을 때 어떻게 맞이해야 할지 늘 고민이었어요.
오늘 선배님께서 '먼 길 오시느라 피곤하셨을 텐데 차 한잔 드세요'라며 상대를 먼저 배려하셨어요.
작은 배려의 말 한마디가 상대방의 긴장을 풀어 주고 신뢰를 쌓는 바탕이 되었어요.
en: I was always worried about how to greet external VIPs when they visited our office.
Today, my senior showed consideration first by saying, 'You must be tired from the long trip, please have a cup of tea.'
A single warm word of consideration relieved the guest's tension and laid the foundation for building trust.

im-c48-04.q: How did the senior greet the visiting guests with consideration?
options: By acknowledging their tiring journey and offering warm tea (피곤하셨을 텐데 차 한잔 드세요)
By immediately demanding a signed contract
By remaining silent and pointing to an empty chair
im-c48-04.why: The text states '먼 길 오시느라 피곤하셨을 텐데 차 한잔 드세요라며 상대를 먼저 배려하셨어요'.

im-c48-04.q: What positive result came from the senior's considerate greeting?
options: It relaxed the visitor's tension and laid a foundation of trust
The meeting was instantly cancelled
The visitor left the building right away
im-c48-04.why: The text explains '상대방의 긴장을 풀어 주고 신뢰를 쌓는 바탕이 되었어요'.
